The story does not have a balance between scene and summary/exposition; instead, it relies exclusively on "scene." Written in the format of a script with only dialogue and brief, present-tense stage directions, the entire narrative unfolds in real-time through character interaction and action. There is no narrative summary to compress time, nor is there direct exposition—all background information (such as the characters' shared history and time spent apart) is implied strictly through the subtext of their conversation.
